interactions.summary: The class connects mountain pilgrimage to purification, and Jiang turns to medieval and Renaissance art to argue that Dante's mathematical and spatial precision helped create a new, more three-dimensional imaginative order.

claims.claim: A student links Purgatory to real pilgrimage routes where bodily ascent and prayer become a form of purification.
Jiang contrasts medieval art with Renaissance art by saying the latter makes space, time, depth, and perspective newly central.
Jiang says Renaissance imaginative power depends on geography, mathematics, symmetry, and precise detail, and he traces that impulse back to Dante.
The class agrees that realistic historical moments and spatially vivid scenes ignite imagination far more powerfully than flatter icon-like imagery.

signature_moments.moment: Dante is recast as the poet who smuggles mathematics and perspective into spiritual imagination so that poetry can feel architectural and inhabitable.
signature_moments.source_phrase: dante is really concerned about mathematics
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It ties Jiang's geolocation argument directly to the birth of Renaissance realism.

chronology_notes.note: The mountain climb becomes an art-historical claim: Dante's precise pilgrimage world trains the kind of spatial imagination later visible in Renaissance painting.
